title: Underwood says the FLIR could not have lost lock; active-duty WSO disagrees

tellings.quote: who's the Wizo who filmed it, he said, "Nope, there's no way the system would have lost it. I've talked to an active duty Wizo serving now and he said it's a finick."

plain: In the 2004 encounter off Southern California with the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint, Chad Underwood, the weapons systems officer (the back-seat crewman, called a "wizzo", who runs a fighter jet's sensors) who filmed it, says his FLIR, an infrared targeting camera, could not have lost its lock on the object, while an active-duty weapons systems officer says the system is finicky. The writer and analyst Marik von Rennenkampff relays both views during a debate on the show about the video with a skeptic. Whether the camera lost lock matters, because a lost lock could explain the object's sudden apparent leap out of view.
